moments.title: Building the pile
moments.text: In a squash court under the west stands of the unused Stagg Field, Enrico Fermi's team began stacking graphite blocks and uranium in round-the-clock shifts.

moments.title: The first chain reaction
moments.text: That afternoon the pile achieved the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction, a key step for the Manhattan Project.

moments.title: Moved to the Argonne Forest
moments.text: The pile was taken apart and rebuilt with shielding as Chicago Pile-2 in the Argonne Forest near Palos Park, where it reached criticality on Mar 20, 1943.

moments.title: Stagg Field's stands come down
moments.text: The old stadium's stands, where the reactor had been, were demolished. The university later built its Regenstein Library on the Stagg Field site.

moments.title: A National Historic Landmark
moments.text: The site of the first self-sustaining nuclear reaction was designated a National Historic Landmark.

moments.title: Henry Moore's Nuclear Energy
moments.text: Exactly 25 years after the experiment, the university unveiled Henry Moore's 12-foot bronze sculpture on the spot.

moments.title: Today: a sculpture by the library
moments.text: Nuclear Energy stands on a small plaza on Ellis Ave, near the Regenstein Library, marking where the reactor stood.

facts.label: Team
facts.note: About four dozen scientists and staff.

checked.notes: Squash court under Stagg Field's west stands; construction from Nov 16, 1942; first self-sustaining chain reaction Dec 2, 1942 (Wikipedia, Atomic Heritage Foundation, OSTI). Dismantled early 1943 (sources say February or March) and rebuilt as CP-2 in the Argonne Forest; CP-2 critical Mar 20, 1943 (Argonne). Stands demolished 1957. NHL Feb 18, 1965 per Wikipedia. Moore's Nuclear Energy unveiled Dec 2, 1967 (University of Chicago, Renaissance Society).
